sentences.text: 4. While pressing the instant application for bail, learned counsel for the appellant submitted that the victim/respondent no. 2 at the behest of one Munna, which is having previous enmity with the co-accused Ayesha W/o Muqaddar Ali (appellant), took benefit of the meeting of Bhartiya Kisan Union (in short "BKU") held on 20.06.2023 of which, at relevant point of time, the co-accused Ayesha D/o Khalil W/o Muqaddar Ali (appellant) was 'Adhyaksha' of Block Bithi of BKU and concocted the story and based upon the same preferred an application dated 10.10.2023 under Section 156(3) Cr.P.C. alleging therein that on 20.06.2023 co-accused Ayesha allured her to induct in the organization namely BKU and therefore, the respondent no. 2 accompanied her to the place where meeting was held and there co-accused Ayesha introduced the respondent no. 2 to Sonu alias Shamshad Ali S/o Ramzan Ali and Muqaddar Ali S/o Amar and also to one unknown person

and while coming back, the respondent no. 2 was on motorcycle of Sonu alias Shamshad Ali and other persons were also on the separate motorcycle(s) and at a tea-stall situated in mid-way, these persons administered some substance and on account of the same, she became unconscious and thereafter all these three persons committed rape with her and when at about three in the night, she became conscious, she found that Ayesha was sleeping with her.
5.

It is further stated that from the aforesaid, it is apparent that after delay of about four months, the application dated 10.10.2023 under Section 156(3) Cr.P.C. was preferred making allegations therein to attract offense under Sections - 376-D, 504, 328 I.P.C. and Section 3(2)(v) of SC/ST Act.
6.
He further stated that taking note of the aforesaid as also the entire facts of the case, it can be deduced that the entire story of the prosecution is completely false and concocted.

The facts indicated are as under:
a) The respondent no. 2 in the application under Section 156(3) Cr.P.C. as also the statement made by her in terms of under Section(s) 161 and 164 Cr.P.C. before police officer and Court concerned, respectively, levelled allegations against co-accused Sonu alias Shamshad Ali S/o Ramzan Ali and upon due investigation, the Investigating Officer on being found his location at Delhi dropped his name and filed the charge-sheet only against Muqaddar Ali S/o Amar, Aman Singh Nishad and Ayesha.
b) Co-accused Ayesha has already been released by the trial Court vide order dated 29.01.2024.
c) The respondent no. 2 admittedly is wife of Ram Prakash and despite this and specific allegations made by the respondent no. 2 to attract offense under Section 376-D IPC, Ram Prakash was not present at the time of medical examination of the victim/respondent no. 2.

sentences.text: d) Committing the crime, as alleged, is not possible by the appellant/Muqaddar Ali in presence of his wife Ayesha/co-accused.

e) For the purpose of medical examination, she was taken the hospital by Constable Anjali Mishra (PNO-192065450) and at relevant point of time along with the respondent no. 2, Munna Khan was present at the hospital.

f) There is enmity between Munna Khan and co-accused Ayesha as between these persons four cases are pending namely i.e. (i) Case Crime No. 36 of 2023 under Sections 354, 504, 506, 376, 458, 323, 419, 420, 467, 468 IPC; (ii) Case Crime No.
134 of 2023 under Section 506 IPC; (iii) Case Crime No. 200 of 2023 under Sections 504, 506 IPC and (iv) Case Crime No. 206 of 2023 under Sections 504, 506 IPC and also one NCR No. 09 of 2023 under Sections 352, 504 IPC.
g) In Case Crime Nos. 200 of 2023, 36 of 2023, 134 of 2023, 206 of 2023,
charge-sheet(s) have already been submitted and investigation in relation to NCR No.
09 of 2023 is going on and all these cases relates to Police Station - Bhiti, District - Ambedkar Nagar.

7. He further submitted that it is apparent from the aforesaid that at the behest of Munna Khan,
present FIR was lodged implicating Ayesha, her husband Muqaddar Ali (appellant), Sonu alias Shamshad Ali and Amar Singh Nishad.

8. He further submitted that medical opinion also does not suggest the crime as indicated by the respondent no. 2.
9.

He last submitted that the appellant, who is in jail since 12.01.2024 and criminal history of the appellant has been explained in para 18 to the rejoinder affidavit, is entitled for bail and the impugned order is liable to be set aside and the appeal is liable to be allowed.

10. Learned A.G.A. and Shri Anil Kumar Tiwari, learned counsel for the respondent no. 2/
complainant vehemently opposed the prayer of the appellant, however, he could not dispute the above contentions made by the appellant's counsel.

11. Shri Anil Kumar Tiwari, learned counsel for the respondent no. 2/ complainant stated that the presence of Munna Khan at the time of medical examination of the victim/complainant/respondent no. 2 would not dilute the act of the appellant, however, he could not dispute that at relevant point of time, the husband of the complainant was not present.
He also could not dispute that the doctor has opined that there is no sign of use of force.

12. Considered the arguments advanced by the learned counsel for the appellant, learned A.G.A. and gone through the contents of the appeal, impugned order, F.I.R., as well as other relevant documents including the statement of the victim recorded under Sections 161 and 164 Cr.P.C.

sentences.text: Upon due consideration of above facts and circumstances including that (i) co-accused Ayesha W/o the appellant has already been released on bail by the trial Court; (ii) possibility of committing the alleged crime by the appellant in presence of his wife; (iii) name of co-accused Sonu alias Shamshad Ali has been dropped as his present was found at Delhi; (iv) presence of Munna Khan at the time of medical medical examination of respondent no. 2/victim and the medical report of the victim and (v) criminal case initiated by co-accused Ayesha against Munna, which are pending and that the appellant is in jail since 12.01.2024 and also that criminal history of the appellant has been explained in para 18 to the rejoinder affidavit and also keeping in view the fact that the trial of the case is not likely to be concluded in near future, this Court is of the view that the appeal has substance and it is accordingly, allowed.

14 . Order dated 16.02.2024 passed by Special Judge, SC/ST Act, Ambedkar Nagar in Bail Application No. 155 of 2024 arising out of Case Crime No. 711 of 2023, under Sections - 376-D, 504,
328 I.P.C. and Section 3(2)(v) of SC/ST Act, P.S. Kotwali Akbarpur, District - Ambedkar Nagar is hereby set aside.

15. Let the appellant Muqaddar Ali be released on bail in the aforesaid case crime number on his furnishing personal bond of Rs. 25,000/- and two reliable sureties each of the like amount to the satisfaction of the court concerned subject to following additional conditions :-
(i) The appellant will cooperate with the prosecution during trial.
(ii) The appellant will not tamper with the evidence during trial.

(iii) The appellant will not pressurize/intimidate the prosecution witness(es).
(iv) The appellant shall not commit an offence.

(v) The appellant shall not directly or indirectly make any inducement, threat or promise to any person acquainted with the facts of the case so as to dissuade him from disclosing such facts to the court or to any police officer or tamper with the evidence.

(vi) The appellant shall remain present before the trial court on each date fixed,
either personally or through counsel.
(vii) The appellant will not seek any adjournment on the dates fixed for evidence when the witnesses are present in court.

(viii) The appellant shall remain present, in person, before the trial court on the dates fixed for recording of statement under Section 313 Cr.P.C.
16.
In case of default of above conditions it shall be open for the trial court to treat it as abuse of liberty of bail and pass orders in accordance with law.
